Commentary.Commentary: So that again was a good game of cricket! Once again we saw, you don't need to have flat pitches to have exciting games, keep something for the bowlers and you have a contest! Anyway, the deciding ODI between these two sides will be played in Vizag, on 29th October. Action begins at 1330 IST, so do join us for it! Until then, goodbye and take care!

MAN OF THE MATCH, MARTIN GUPTILL, says that it is a wonderful feeling to perform in a winning cause. Feels that everyone's ability in the Kiwi team to fight till the end is admirable and they all felt that 260 was defendable. On Virat Kohli, he admits that he is a classy player and his wicket really boosted their confidence. But he stresses that the team strived to get the other wickets as well. On being asked whether he thought his score would end up being the highest in the match, he laughs and shakes his head but also says he will take it.

New Zealand captain, KANE WILLIAMSON begins by stating that it was an improved effort. Admits that it was not an easy surface and scoring 260 was not a bad effort. On the toss, he adds that dew may or may not come and also the pitch slowing down was a bit confusing but is happy that it worked in their favour. Credits his team for executing their plans well but adds that there is room for improvement. Mentions that they have played on a variety of pitches and all of that factors in during selections. Ends by saying that they will look to adapt to the conditions in Vizag and the guys are looking forward to the decider.

Indian skipper, MAHENDRA SINGH DHONI admits that the first 10 overs were the crucial point where India conceded a lot of runs. Also feels that they gave a bit too many extras. But is happy with the fight shown by the Indian lower order while batting. He opines that the wicket was best to bat on in the afternoon but got slower and slower as the day progressed. Further, he adds that run scoring was best against the new balls as it was difficult to bat once the balls got older. Feels that the batsmen in the batting order 5-7 are still inexperienced and will get the game awareness once they play a few more matches. Does not want them to curb their attacking instincts and feels that with experience, they will learn and serve India for a long period of time. On the dew, he feels that it has not had a great impact so far in this series and would like to see what takes place at Vizag. Ends by saying that such losses and the ones in Delhi keep on happening and the Kiwis are a very good side. Also says that India need to be at their best to win the final ODI.

Earlier in the day, New Zealand once again huffed and puffed up past the 250-run mark after getting a good start. Guptill was the star for them scoring 72 but once he was dismissed, the Kiwis struggled to get going. The spinners in Jadhav, Patel and Mishra bowled well between them to keep New Zealand to 260 but in the end, it proved to be enough.

Hardik Pandya again fell to a glory shot and despite some late rearguard action from Umesh Yadav and Dhawal Kulkarni, they could not stop the visitors from registering their second win on the tour. Tim Southee finished with best figures for New Zealand in the game, he took 3/40. He along with Trent Boult and Jimmy Neesham took 7 wickets in all which is opposite to what worked for India earlier in the day. The Indian pacers only managed to take three wickets between them.

India did lose Rohit early but Rahane held one end up. Kohli again looked good but was snapped up by Ish Sodhi. Plenty of dots followed and the pressure got the better of the Indian batsmen. Rahane failed to convert his start and Dhoni failed to get going and the young batsmen in Pandey, Kedar departed in quick succession to hand the advantage to New Zealand.

Phew! Another thriller! The series is alive and kicking! New Zealand have again defended a slightly below par score to perfection. The ODI series has gone down the wire and that is a welcome change from the Tests! On a pitch that was difficult one to score quickly, the Kiwis were brilliant with the ball and have managed to stay alive in the series with a win here at Ranchi.

OUT! NEW ZEALAND WIN BY 19 RUNS AND LEVEL THE SERIES 2-2! Boult gets the final wicket. A length ball outside off, Umesh looks to give this the big swing. But because the pitch is a bit slow, the ball does not come on to the bat that easily. He miscues it to short extra cover where Ross Taylor takes a simple catch. So we will have a series finale in Vizag.
On a good length outside off, angling in, dabbed down to third man for one.
Full and wide outside off, blasted down to long off for a run.
Landed outside off, guided to third man for a single.
Landed outside off, swung away to widish long on for another single.

A slower ball on middle, on a length, Yadav is early into his pull and miscues it towards deep mid-wicket. One run. The stand moves to 30 from 32 balls. India still not giving up hope. Excellent rearguard action.
Full and outside off, blasted to mid off who is pretty deep. A run taken.
Another slower ball, around off, punched back to the bowler who parries it to short extra cover.
Around off, defended towards short mid-wicket.
Mid-wicket comes in for Dhawal.

TIM SOUTHEE to bowl now, his penultimate over.
On a length on off, Dhawal pushes it towards point off his crease. India need 27 runs in 18 balls.
FOUR! Hit away! On a length outside off, Kulkarni cuts it past the diving Devcich at point for a boundary. Crucial hit, that!
WIDE! Bowls this slower one down the leg side. A wide is signaled.
Angled in on a length on off, Umesh taps it towards mid off and takes a quick single.
A touch short outside off, Kulkarni arches back and dabs it to third man for a single.
Good length outside off, Kulkarni gives himself room and defends it towards point.
Good length on off, Umesh punches it towards covers for a single and gets off strike.
TRENT BOULT to bowl from around the wicket.
Bowls a quicker one on the stumps, Kulkarni keeps it out. India need 35 more in 24 balls.
FOUR! In the gap! Shorter outside off, Kulkarni gets on top of it and cuts it hard through point for a boundary. Vital boundary for India!
Dhawal watches the ball turn away from him and adjusts well to defend it towards gully.
Bowls it too full on off, Dhawal just about manages to keep it out.
Shorter outside off, Umesh stands tall and punches it through covers for a single.
Floated outside off, Dhawal heaves it off the inner half for a single to mid-wicket.
WIDE! Sprays it wide outside offf, Dhawal is calm as he lets that one go.
Shorter outside off, worked through mid-wicket for a single to keep the strike. 9 runs off the over! India need 42 more runs in 30 balls.
Fuller outside off, Dhawal looks to go big but ends up hitting it in the air over backward point. Guptill gets across and stops the ball in time and keeps them to a couple.
Quicker one on middle, Dhawal mistimes his punch back down the wicket.
Dhawal goes for another heave but fails to put bat to ball.
Tossed up outside off, Kulkarni plays inside the line of that one and is beaten.
SIX! Take that, Sodhi! Fuller outside off, Kulkarni comes forward and lofts it over the long off for a maximum.

STUMPING APPEAL but nothing in it. Full and wide outside off, Umesh has a wild slog but misses. Watling takes the ball and whips off the bails and appeals. However, the square leg umpire is confident and does not even bother to go upstairs. Replays show that it is close but the foot is in.
Another edge, this time the outside one. Tossed up invitingly outside off, DK has a wild slog but gets a thick outside edge which goes through the vacant slip region to short third man. A run taken.
Slowly tossed up outside off, Dhawal has a big hoick but gets a bottom edge which misses the stumps en route to short fine leg.
Full and outside off, slogged to deep mid-wicket for a run.
On middle and leg, flicked through square leg for a single. Gets off the mark.
Full and outside off, defended watchfully.
SANTNER comes back on to bowl.
On middle and off, defended watchfully. 3 runs and 2 wickets from that over!
A full toss outside off, Umesh throws the kitchen sink at that but misses. The ball shoots up after pitching and Watling does well to collect it at his face.
Full and around off, swinging in, defended back to the bowler.

BOWLED! That is a ripper! Full on middle, Axar looks to flick but is beaten by the pace. The ball hits his pads and rockets onto the off stump. Two wickets in the space of 4 balls for the Kiwis. INDIA NEED 54 FROM 45 BALLS WITH 1 WICKET IN HAND!
WIDE and a single! Slower ball gone awry, full and down the leg side, Dhawal misses his flick and Bradley Watling fumbles, conceding the single.
A length  ball around off, tapped towards point. Kulkarni wants the single but is sent back.

OUT! Mishra is run out! Total miscommunication. A short ball on middle, Axar pulls it through mid-wicket and sets off for a single. There is an easy two available and Mishra charges back and so does Axar. But then he says no as he is not confident that he can get back in time. However, Mishra does not listen at all and keeps on running. In the meanwhile, Mitchell Santner gets across to his left and slides to return a decent throw to Watling who makes no mistake in disturbing the stumps. Mishra is furious with Axar and walks back in frustration. The enterprising 38-run stand is broken.
BOULT back on for a bowl.
Outside off, dabbed to point for a single.
Short and outside off, Axar jumps and cuts it on the bounce to point.
Half volley on middle and leg, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
SIX! Handsome! Full and around off, Axar comes forward and lofts it straight back over the bowler and it lands near the sightscreen! 200 UP FOR INDIA, 58 needed from 51 now!
Full and wide outside off, lofted wide of extra cover for a run. The stand moves to 30 from 32 balls. Crucial one for India.
Full on middle, pushed down to long on for a single.
Another bowling change! Neesham into the attack now. There was a mini-conference between Neesham, Southee and Williamson.
Short ball around off, dragged wide of Tim Southee at long on for a couple.
Landed outside off, Mishra looks to play the reverse sweep but the ball hits his gloves and goes on the bounce to the keeper. Rohit Sharma has a laugh in the dressing room on seeing that.

OVERTHROW! Unlucky for New Zealand. Full and around off, Mishra sweeps this powerfully through mid-wicket. The fielder gets to the ball quickly and returns a fast throw, but to his dismay, it hits the stumps at the striker's end directly and deflects to point. Mishra is aware of the situation and charges for the second. 68 more needed from 56 balls now!
Landed outside off, Amit opens the face of the bat and guides it to third man. Sets off for the single but is sent back.
Full and outside leg, swept down to fine leg but short fine leg gets across to stop. A run taken.
Growing in confidence is Mishra, comes down the track and hits this down to long on for a single. Moves to 10 from 12 balls. Much sensible batting as opposed to that in Delhi.
Ish Sodhi back on for a bowl.
Powerplay 3 has been signaled, five fielders are now allowed outside the circle for the last ten overs.
On middle and leg, gently nudged through square leg for a run. 10 from the over!
FOUR! Lovely batting! This game is not over yet. Full on middle, Mishra comes forward and across and works it wide of mid on. The fielder dives to his right but the ball goes through!
Outside off, dabbed to third man for a run.

MISFIELD! FOUR! Short and outside off, Axar punches it through the covers. The ball races away but Mitchell Santner covers good from sweeper cover to his left and slides. However, he takes his eyes off the ball and it goes through! 78 more needed from 63 balls now.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
Full and straight, defended towards short mid-wicket.
TIM SOUTHEE comes back for a spell. He has taken three wickets already and will be looking to wrap this up early.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Outside off, steered behind point to third man for a run.
Full and outside off, driven on the bounce to the bowler who leaps to stop.
On the pads, Amit misses his tuck and the ball goes off his pads towards square leg. A leg bye taken.
Walks across his stumps and lets a bouncer go. He then asks the umpire why it wasn't a wide. We don't know what the umpire said but as far as we saw, the ball went over leg stump.
Outside off, dabbed to third man for a single. The stand moves to 10 from 13 balls.
On middle, tapped to the leg side for a quick single.

The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. Two runs added to the total. Mishra dives in to make his ground. Axar moves to 20 from 24 balls. He is very critical player for India from here on. Needs partners.

NOT OUT! Just one replay confirms that the ball has bounced. Landed outside off, Axar looks to play the pull shot but bottom edges it onto his pads. The ball lobs up and Watling comes forward, fumbles once but then dives to take on the second. He appeals and the umpires confer and then refer it to the third umpire. The soft signal is out but the replays confirm otherwise.
Another third umpire referral! The Kiwis are confident here. They reckon they have Axar caught and umpire Bruce Oxenford has nodded his head too. What will the replays show? Let us see...
Full and outside off, Mishra paddle-pulls this towards short fine leg for a run.
Lovely stop. Landed outside off, pretty full, Mishra gently opens the face of the bat and guides it to third man but Ross Taylor at first slip dives to his right to stop the ball.
Landed around off, spinning in, worked through mid-wicket for a single. 89 more needed from 77 balls now.
ISH SODHI back on for a bowl.
The batsman guides it to third man. They pick up a single.
A length ball outside off, chopped down to third man for one.
Outside off, steered down to third man for a run.
A short ball outside off, steered aerially to third man for a single. Gets off the mark.
Outside off, angling away, Amit pushes but misses.
A bouncer on middle, Mishra ducks.
AMIT MISHRA is the new man in.

OUT! That is another spectacular catch by Tom Latham! Flighted on middle and off, Pandya comes down the track and looks to go inside out. The shot selection is good, so is the timing but perhaps the power is a bit less. He hits this towards extra cover but Tom Latham covers plenty of ground from long off to his left and takes a very good catch, just inside the ropes. Pandya is down on his knees. Fuller outside off, Axar comes forward and pushes it to covers.
TRENT BOULT called back on for a bowl.
DRINKS BREAK!
Fuller outside off, Pandya comes forward and pushes it to covers. India need 102 more in 96 balls!
Gets across and works it towards square leg for a single.

Fuller otside off, Pandey guides it towards point where Guptill dives to his right and stops the ball. That was superbly done.

Fuller on off, Patel clips it through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Back of a length angling in, Pandey guides it down to third man for a single.
FOUR! Strong wrists from Pandey! Fuller outside off, Pandey gets down on it in quick time and slams it through mid off for a boundary. That was hit hard.
Pandey comes forward and pushes it towards mid on.

Dhoni pushes it for a single to deep point.
Dhoni keeps this one out.

OUT! NEESHAM STRIKES! Angles it on a fuller length on middle, Rahane looks to get across and clip it through. He though is hit on his pads. Outside off on a length, Rahane guides it down to third man for a couple of runs. Southee did well from third man to keep the ball in play with a fine dive.

Dhoni comes forward and again drives it to covers off his crease.

Floated on middle, Dhoni comes forward and defends it.

Dhoni drives it through mid off for a single.
This time Rahane comes forward, taps it to covers and Dhoni responds for the quick single. Rahane signals for a change of gloves.
Floated outside off, Rahane pushes it through point but not in the gap.
Tossed up on off, Rahane comes forward and pushes it to covers. He looks for a single but is sent back.

Shorter on off, Rahane punches it back down the wicket for a single. India need 139 runs in 150 balls.

Drives it through mid off for a single.

Flatter on the pads, Dhoni comes down and tucks it towards mid-wicket.

Dhoni comes down to play the big shot but finds himself out of place and pushes it to covers.
Rahane turns it through square leg for a single.
WIDE! Bowls it way outside off, left alone again. Another wide.
Fuller on middle, Rahane keeps it out.
Rahane looks to work it towards the on side but does not connect well.
WIDE! Sprays it wide outside off. Left alone. A wide is signaled.

Dhoni comes forward and pushes it to covers.
Short on middle, worked towards the on side.
Floated outside off, Dhoni looks to drive but seems to have missed it. The keeper collects and appeals along with the bowler but the umpire says no.
Shorter outside off, left alone by Dhoni.
Dhoni comes forward and pushes it towards cover-point. Slight hesitation on the run.
Floated outside off, Dhoni comes forward and defends it with his bat and pad together.
Flatter down the leg side, Rahane looks to clip it away. The ball goes off the pads.

Flatter on middle, Dhoni defends it back down the wicket.
Fuller outside off, Dhoni slinks down and turns it back to the bowler.

Flatter on middle, Rahane tucks it down to fine leg for a couple of runs.

MS Dhoni again walks in at number 4! He walks in with loud cheers.

Edged! Floated outside off, Kohli looks to defend but gets an inside edge towards the on side.

A slip in place now.

Fuller outside off, Kohli drives it through mid off.

That is a high full toss outside off, smashed past the bowler down the ground. Mitchell Santner comes running in to his right from long off and dives full length to save the boundary. Two more to the total.
MISFIELD! Full and outside off, Kohli pushes this straight to backward point but Ross Taylor gets across to his left and tumbles, allowing the ball to go through. Two runs taken.

Short on middle, punched down to long on for one. India won't mind this at all. Easy singles on offer.
Outside off, punched through the covers for a run.

EDGED, BUT NO SLIP IN PLACE! Full and around off, Rahane looks to work it to the leg side but the ball spins away, takes the outside edge, through the vacant slip region to short third man. A run taken.
Around off, short in length, punched straight to short extra cover.
Outside off, guided towards short third man for a single.

SIX! Lovely shot! Flighted outside off, Kohli comes forward and lofts this inside out over long off for a biggie!
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
The batsman has attempted to put bat on ball - but fails.
50-run stand up between Kohli and Rahane!
On middle, pushed down to long on for a single.

Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full toss outside off, driven straight to Martin Guptill at short extra cover.

FOUR! That will be a boundary! Landed outside off, Kohli goes back and opens the face of his bat at the last moment to beat short third man! Tim Southee runs after the ball, tries to do a repeat of what Boult did on the previous ball but slides with the ball into the ropes!

Great effort from Trent Boult. Short on middle, Kohli goes back and whips it over mid-wicket. Trent Boult gets across from mid-wicket and slides to his left to push the ball away. However, while doing so, his feet touch the ropes and it is referred upstairs. Now, this is interesting. Replays show that Boult initially kicked the ropes away, but then while pushing the ball away, his left leg was in the air while the right foot was not touching the ropes. Close call. Two runs signalled.

How did that miss the stumps? Lucky escape for Rahane. A short ball outside off, Rahane looks to pull but gets a bottom edge which misses the off stump!
Outside off, steered to third man for a run.
Gets across and clips it straight to short mid-wicket.
Short and outside off, Ajinkya goes to cut but gets a bottom edge to the off side. A quick single.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. One run added to the total.

Simon Doull on air nicely explains how Jimmy Neesham is falling over as he gets to his crease to bowl and hence is bowling the wides. He reckons Neesham could look up to Southee and work on his delivery stride.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.
WIDE. Down the leg side, Rahane misses his flick.
Short and outside off, cut through point for a single. Not a bad start from Santner at all. 209 more needed from 234 balls.
Slow, loopy ball outside off, defended watchfully.
Outside off, guided straight to short third man.

Short again, this time around off, Kohli plays it from the stumps towards point and takes off for the single. Nearly collides with Rahane but they avert each other and make it safely to the other end.
Shortish on middle, whipped straight to short mid-wicket.

Good start. Santner flights this around off, gets Kohli forward to defend but then makes it spin away to beat the outside edge. Maybe Williamson can get a slip in for Santner. If he gets Kohli early, India will be under pressure.
Time for some spin! MITCHELL SANTNER to bowl now.
POWERPLAY 2 has been signalled. Four fielders allowed outside the 30-yard circle till the 40th over now.
On middle and leg, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
WIDE. 50 UP FOR INDIA. Down the leg side, Rahane misses his flick.
Full and outside off, driven sweetly but straight to short extra cover.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman.
On middle and leg, Jinx works it to the left of Southee at short fine leg, comes halfway down the track for what should have been an easy single but Kohli is not sure so sends him back.
Outside off, Rahane fishes and misses.
Down the leg side, helped through fine leg. Rahane calls Kohli through for a quick single as Tim Southee dives to his right to stop the ball. The stand moves to 30 from 30 balls.
First change, JIMMY NEESHAM to bowl now.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
FOUR! Nicely controlled. A short ball around off, Rahane pulls it all along the ground and gets it through backward square leg. Ish Sodhi runs to his left from fine leg and dives but misses!

Gets across his stumps to flick but Southee has literally bowled a fast off spinner there. It lands on a shortish length outside off and it spins past the pad and leg stump to the keeper. No wide signalled and Kohli at the non-striker's end smiles. He moved a bit across, did Rahane, hence no signal for the wide.

UPPISH, SAFE! FOUR! Full and outside off, Rahane leans and drives it in the air, but wide of the man at short cover and through to the fence! 217 more needed from 249 balls now. Rahane moves to 21 from 18 balls.
A lovely slower ball outside off, fuller in length, Rahane is sucked into the drive but gets a thick inside edge onto the pads.
Outside off, dabbed straight to Ross Taylor at gully.
Excellent comeback by the bowler. On a good length outside off, Kohli looks to work it to the leg side but it swings back in after pitching and cuts him into two!

FOUR! One won't see too many better shots than that. On a good length around middle, Kohli gets back and works it with the wrists wide of mid on for a boundary! Moves to 10 from 17 balls. The stand moves to 21 from 22 balls.
Outside off, defended straight to gully.
Full on middle and off, swinging in, defended with a straight bat back to the bowler.
Around off, worked through mid-wicket for a run.
Landed outside off, guided down to third man for a single.
Full and outside off, Ajinkya works it towards short mid-wicket.
Around off, worked to the leg side.
A good bouncer outside off, Rahane bails out of the pull.
Around off, nicely guided past Ross Taylor at gully to third man for a single.
Full and outside off, Kohli gets across, walks forward and defends it to the off side.
Stays back in his crease and defends.

SIX! What a shot! That too from Rahane! Short and outside off, Rahane jumps and cuts it over point and gets it to go all the way! 11 from the over! 228 more needed from 264 balls now. This stand is worth 14 from 11 balls.
Excellent fielding! Full and wide outside off, Rahane leans and drives it through point but Martin Guptill dives to his right to stop the ball. Brilliant.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

FOUR! Glorious! Full and outside off, Rahane comes forward and drives it wide of mid off. Kane Williamson (if my colleague is to be believed) dives to his left but the ball goes through! Rahane moves to 10 from 8 balls.
Outside off, steered behind point for a single.
Landed outside off, Kohli stays back in his crease and defends.

Gets across his stumps and looks to tuck it away but misses and is hit on the pads. No appeal from the Kiwis, perhaps they thought it would be going down leg. 3 runs and a wicket from the over, Southee has figures of 3-0-11-1.
Full on middle, pushed between mid on and mid-wicket for a single. 239 more needed from 271 balls.
On middle and leg, Kohli works it through square leg and gets a couple to move off the mark.
Around off, worked gently towards short mid-wicket.
Outside off, comes back in, left alone.
VIRAT KOHLI walks in at Number 3.

OUT! Caught behind! Southee strikes early! On a good length outside off, Rohit pushes at it. The ball moves away a bit and takes a thin outside edge to Bradley Watling. Rohit fails again. INDIA NEED 242 FROM 275 BALLS WITH 9 WICKETS IN HAND.
Outside off, tapped to third man for a single.
Around off, pushed through point where Martin Guptill dives to his right and stops it.
The slower ball, fuller in length, around off, watchfully defended.
Goes round the wicket!
FOUR! Back-to-back! A length ball outside off, slightly wide, Rohit crunches this in front of point and gets successive boundaries! Moves to 10 from 15 balls.
FOUR! Nicely done. A short ball on middle and leg, Rohit just helps it behind square leg, one bounce and into the ropes! 247 more needed from 280 balls now.
Outside off, punched straight to short extra cover.
On middle and leg, worked behind square leg for a run.
Down the leg side, Sharma misses his tuck and the ball goes off his pads towards fine leg. Ish Sodhi does a good sliding stop at the fence to keep the batsmen to a couple. Leg byes signalled.
That is a beauty! On a good length outside off, Rohit is squared up as he tries to defend it from his crease. The ball moves away and beats the outside edge.
On middle and leg, worked towards fine leg for a single.
On a good length this time, pushed away from the body towards cover.
Nice and straight, slightly full, defended to the off side.
Outside off, RS guides it off the edge, on the bounce, towards the diving Ross Taylor at first slip. A MAIDEN FROM BOULT!
Full and wide outside off, Sharma has a loose waft and misses.
Back of a length on middle, worked straight to square leg.
Angled away outside off, Rohit shoulders his arms to let it through.
Fuller in length, swinging in, defensively patted towards point.
On middle and leg, worked straight to short mid-wicket.
TRENT BOULT to bowl with the second new ball.
FOUR! That is through! On a length outside off, Rahane punches this on the up through cover-point and gets the first boundary of the run chase!
Landed outside off, Ajinkya shoulders arms.
On middle and leg, shorter in length, worked through square leg for a run. 259 more needed from 296 balls now.
Fuller in length this time, outside off, watchfully tapped away.
Outside off, tapped towards point.
India are away. On a length on middle, Rahane works it through square leg for a single.

Welcome back for the chase! The two Indian openers, ROHIT SHARMA and AJINKYA RAHANE are out in the middle. Will they attack the new balls like the visitors did? Let's see. New Zealand begin with Tim Southee! Here we go...
